title: Edmund and the Passage
premise: Felix Nakamura, estranged child of a disgraced archaeologist and a better digger than their father ever was, survives by moving—between digs, towns, and identities. When a record-low tide exposes a sea cave that local legend says charges admission, Felix is pulled into a decades-old disappearance and a river that runs upstream to a forbidden source beneath a glacier. Chased by a family that calls its violence justice, Felix must reach the source before calving season opens—and destroys—the route. They find their father's last secret there, choose mercy over vengeance, and finally stop running.
about_author: Casper Fairweather is the pen name of a former field assistant on glaciology surveys who traded academic life for storytelling after a near-miss on an ice sheet. They write adventure fiction about people who are better at surviving than living.

chapters.title: The Tide Keeps Books
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In a fading fishing town, Felix waits out a record-low tide, digging shell middens for cash and refusing an offer to join a university survey. The beat is restless competence—Felix reads the shore like a ledger and knows every entry is temporary.

chapters.title: What the Water Returns
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The tide drops farther than anyone alive has seen, revealing a cave mouth beneath the headland. Inside, Felix finds a rusted lantern, a woman's boot, and a carved stone bearing their father's mark. The beat is dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: Admission
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Locals warn that the cave 'takes payment'—three climbers vanished in 1987, the year Felix's father led an expedition. That night someone ransacks Felix's room, taking nothing but the carved stone. The beat is the past arriving with a bill.

chapters.title: The Nakamura Name
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix flees town but is intercepted by Maren Voss, daughter of one of the vanished climbers, who has spent thirty years hunting the truth. She offers partnership and an old map. The beat is wary alliance between two people who distrust everyone.

chapters.title: A River That Runs Wrong
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren explains the legend: the cave's stream flows from a source high on the Vinter Glacier, a route the ice opens for only weeks each decade. Her father's last letter named Felix's father. The beat is a map becoming a debt.

chapters.title: The Family That Collects
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A man called Alder Voss—Maren's cousin, enforcer for the family's private 'justice' over the vanished expedition—finds them. He wants the map and the stone, and he wants Felix to confess what their father took. The beat is menace in polite clothing.

chapters.title: Running Water, Running People
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix and Maren escape Alder by following the cave stream inland, discovering it runs beneath the town and emerges impossibly far uphill. The beat is wonder and fear braided together—the land itself is lying to them.

chapters.title: The Digger's Hands
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren watches Felix work—reading soil, bracing a collapse, saving them both—and realizes the rumors were true: the child out-dug the father. She admits she needs Felix, not just the map. The beat is grudging respect turning to trust.

chapters.title: Provisions and Lies
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In a supply town, they buy gear and learn Alder has posted a story about them: thieves, wanted by the family, not the law. Felix recognizes the tactic—make the law irrelevant. The beat is the first taste of being hunted by narrative.

chapters.title: The Old Route
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. They reach the trailhead her father described: a river gorge that narrows into the glacier's tongue. A wrecked basecamp from 1987 still stands, tagged with the family's justice-marks. The beat is walking into a preserved crime scene.

chapters.title: Camp of the Vanished
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Among the ruins Felix finds their father's field journal, water-damaged, pages torn out. Entries describe the source, a find worth killing for, and a line that stops Felix cold: 'If anything happens, it was my idea, not the boy's.' The beat is grief ambushing them mid-task.

chapters.title: Alder's Sermon
chapters.summary: Alder's POV. Alder catches up and, over a fire, explains the family creed: the law failed the dead, so the family judges. He offers Felix a walk away and Maren a trial. The beat is conviction that is almost persuasive—and entirely merciless.

chapters.title: The First Crossing
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A rope traverse over the gorge river goes wrong; Felix nearly drowns saving Maren's map case, then admits it was the map, not her, they reached for first. The beat is honesty as a form of intimacy.

chapters.title: Ice That Remembers
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The glacier's edge exposes a body in the ice—decades old, wearing a 1987 expedition tag. Maren recognizes the jacket as her father's spare. The beat is hope curdling into certainty that the dead are closer than legend claimed.

chapters.title: The Torn Pages
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix reconstructs the journal's missing pages from memory of their father's habits and finds the confession: the 'find' at the source was evidence the expedition's financier had murdered a rival—and the father buried it to protect the family name. The beat is the price of survival, itemized.

chapters.title: Whose Justice
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren realizes the family's 'justice' has always been cover for the financier's heirs—her own kin—erasing the murder. She and Felix argue: expose it, or bury it as her father chose. The beat is love against duty, first collision.

chapters.title: The Calving Bell
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A distant crack like a cathedral bell: the glacier has begun its season. The route's window is open—and closing. They push on with Alder a day behind. The beat is the clock becoming a character.

chapters.title: The Hanging Valley
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. A grueling ascent to the hanging valley where the river emerges from the ice. Storm forces them into a crevasse shelter where they find a second journal—the financier rival's—hidden in 1987. The beat is two confessions converging.

chapters.title: Two Confessions
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Reading the rival's journal by headlamp, they learn the murder was ordered by Maren's grandfather, and Felix's father witnessed it. Both their parents were hostages of the same secret. The beat is inherited guilt, shared at last.

chapters.title: Alder at the Icefall
chapters.summary: Alder's POV. Alder crosses the icefall alone, losing a teammate to a crevasse he chose not to rope. His creed wobbles for one page: was it justice, or arithmetic? The beat is a villain's hairline fracture.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. They reach the source: a blue cathedral of ice around a spring, and sealed within it, the proof—documents and the rival's remains, preserved. The cave 'admission' was the glacier's own toll. The beat is awe with a body in it.

chapters.title: What Father Took
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix understands finally: their father didn't steal a treasure—he stole the evidence to keep a family from destroying itself, and paid with exile and estrangement. Felix weeps for the first time in the book. The beat is grief becoming inheritance.

chapters.title: The Trial on the Ice
chapters.summary: Alder's POV. Alder arrives and convenes, alone, the family's judgment on the glacier: Maren for betrayal, Felix for the father's sins. Maren refuses the frame—she demands the family be tried instead. The beat is justice outside the law turned on itself.

chapters.title: The Ice Gives Way
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The calving begins. The source chamber starts to collapse; the evidence, the bodies, the whole archive will fall into the meltwater and be gone. Alder must choose: seize the proof or save people. The beat is the land forcing every hand.

chapters.title: Admission Paid
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. In the collapse, Alder saves Maren instead of the documents—paying, at last, the cave's real price. He is badly injured. The beat is the enforcer's first act of grace, and it costs him everything he used to be.

chapters.title: Descent of the River
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. They ride the flood as the glacier releases the river, the evidence lost to the water forever. Felix lets it go—no archive, no trial, no proof. The beat is terrible release: survival chosen over vindication.

chapters.title: What Survives Is Story
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Stranded below the glacier, they realize the only evidence left is testimony: theirs, and Alder's if he'll give it. Maren decides the family can be faced without proof if the story is told together. The beat is fragile resolve.

chapters.title: The Long Walk Down
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Carrying Alder on a litter through the gorge, the three former enemies negotiate, hour by hour, what truth will be told and who will bear it. The beat is justice rebuilt as a shared burden instead of a verdict.

chapters.title: The Town That Kept the Ledger
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. They return to the fishing town and tell the families of the vanished everything, including the ugly parts. Some forgive; some don't. The beat is truth as a door that opens both ways.

chapters.title: Alder's Account
chapters.summary: Alder's POV. Alder formally dissolves the family's private justice before the assembled town, naming his grandfather's crime and his own. He expects exile and accepts it. The beat is a man sentencing himself.

chapters.title: The Cave at High Tide
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The tide has returned; the cave is sealed again, its admission collected. Felix stands before it and finally answers the question the book opened with—what their father's mark meant: not a claim, an apology. The beat is closure without a grave.

chapters.title: Terms of Staying
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren asks Felix to stay—not as debt or duty, but as choice. Felix, who has never stopped moving, is terrified more by staying than by any glacier. The beat is love against the habit of flight.

chapters.title: The Dig They Stay For
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix takes the university survey job they refused in chapter one—on their own terms, cataloguing the town's middens, teaching local kids to read the shore. The beat is stillness learned as a skill.

chapters.title: Letters Upstream
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix writes to their estranged father for the first time in years: not forgiveness, not accusation—just the truth of what they found, and that the debt is paid. The beat is a letter as a bridge built from one side.

chapters.title: Maren's Inheritance
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren reclaims her family's records and begins a public history of the 1987 expedition—narrative as the only surviving evidence. The beat is justice redefined as remembrance.

chapters.title: Alder's Road
chapters.summary: Alder's POV. Recovering, Alder leaves to carry the confession to the family's scattered branches, a penance and a mission. He and Felix part with a nod that holds everything unsaid. The beat is a villain's exit as a pilgrim's departure.

chapters.title: The Calving Season Ends
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Winter closes the glacier; the route is gone for another decade. Felix watches the ice from the headland and feels, for the first time, no pull to chase a window. The beat is peace with impermanence.

chapters.title: What the Father Sent Back
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A reply arrives: a single page in the father's hand, and inside it, the torn journal pages he kept all these years—returned so Felix can choose what to do with them. Felix donates them, unredacted, to Maren's archive. The beat is the last secret surrendered.

chapters.title: Edmund's Stone
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren reveals the carved stone's origin: 'Edmund' was the rival's name, and her father cut the mark as a promise to remember. The legend's admission was always meant to be memory. The beat is the title's meaning arriving late and landing fully.

chapters.title: The Passage
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, final chapter. A year on, Felix stands at the cave mouth at low tide with Maren, no longer running, and walks in as the water returns—willingly, to place a memorial plaque where the glacier kept its dead. They stop moving; the story stops with them. The beat is arrival: survival paid for, justice shared, love chosen.
